newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-May 15.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- The office of post-handover leader Tung Chee-hwa will unveil the bill to amend two Hong Kong civil liberties ordinances after China takes back the territory on July 1. Tung has arranged to meet representatives of five major political parties to persuade them to support the bill.
-- SING TAO DAILY -- Tung said the territory's US$19 billion Land Fund would operate independently under the supervision of a committee headed by Financial Secretary Donald Tsang.
-- WEN WEI PO -- Chinese Vice-Premier Qian Qichen stressed that ministries and provinces should not interfere in Hong Kong's internal affairs after the handover.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin met a delegation led by Hong Kong businessman Henry Fok and stressed that carrying out the Basic Law, Beijing's post-handover constitution for Hong Kong, was China's long-term policy.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- The Hang Seng Index surged 1.77 percent, largely because U.S. credit rating agency Standard & Poor's raised its sovereign ratings for China and Hong Kong. Experts said the borrowing costs for Hong Kong and Chinese companies might drop by five to 10 percent.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Mainland financial regulators shocked the broking industry with a package of unusually severe punishments against four of China's best known and largest brokerages for manipulating the market.
-- Mainland traders said authorities in Beijing had removed Zhou Daojing as head of the China Securities Regulatory Commission and installed conservative securities expert Zhou Zhenqing in his place.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Another 150 People's Liberation Army soldiers will enter Hong Kong this month without formal ceremony. They will join 40 others already in Hong Kong to prepare British bases throughout the territory for the arrival of the future Chinese garrison.
-- Five major air carriers banded together to offer joint facilities at the new Chek Lap Kok airport in a bid to cut costs and grab a huge bite of the Asian passenger market.
